      action_chunk: ${actor.model.num_action_chunks}
      num_steps: ${actor.model.num_steps}
      train_expert_only: True
      action_env_dim: ${actor.model.action_dim}
      noise_method: "flow_sde"
      add_value_head: ${actor.model.add_value_head}
      pi05: True
      value_after_vlm: True
      value_vlm_mode: "mean_token"

  optim:
    lr: 5.0e-6
    value_lr: 1.0e-4
    adam_beta1: 0.9
    adam_beta2: 0.95
    adam_eps: 1.0e-05
    clip_grad: 1.0
    critic_warmup_steps: 0

  fsdp_config:                  # below are fsdp configs, for more details, see https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/fsdp.html and https://huggingface.co/docs/accelerate/package_reference/fsdp

    strategy: "fsdp"            # FSDP strategy: ["fsdp", "fsdp2"]

    # Sharding strategy: "full_shard" (shard parameters, gradients, optimizer states),
    # "shard_grad_op" (shard gradients and optimizer states only), 
    # "hybrid_shard" (combines data parallelism and model parallelism - sharding within FSDP groups, replicate across DDP groups),
    # "no_shard" (no sharding)
    sharding_strategy: "full_shard" 

    cpu_offload: False           # whether to offload parameters and gradients to CPU when not in use，if True, actor's enable_offload should be True too.
    offload_pin_memory: False    # whether FSDP2's CPU offload policy should pin memory when cpu_offload is True
    reshard_after_forward: True  # if True, FSDP2 will reshard parameters after forward pass to save memory

    enable_gradient_accumulation: True  # if True, gradient accumulation will be enabled for FSDP/FSDP2 training, which will enhance training performance but increase memory usage.
    forward_prefetch: False             # if True, FSDP will explicitly prefetches the next upcoming all-gather while executing in the forward pass. only use with static graphs. Overlaps communication with computation to improve performance.
    limit_all_gathers: False            # if True, FSDP will synchronizes CPU threads to limit the number of concurrent all-gathers. Only affects strategies that schedule all-gathers
    backward_prefetch: null             # options are null, 'pre', 'post'. if 'pre', FSDP will prefetch the next upcoming all-gather while computing gradients. if 'post', FSDP will prefetch the next all-gather until current gradient is computed.
    use_orig_params: False              # if True, FSDP will use module's original parameters, it means it will expose nn.Module.named_parameters rather than FlatParameter
    use_liger_kernel: False             # if True, liger_kernel will be used for FSDP, note that currently supported models in RLinf are [qwen2.5, qwen2.5-vl], for more details, see liger_kernel's doc

    fsdp_size: -1               # Number of GPUs per FSDP group for hybrid sharding. -1 means use all available GPUs in a single FSDP group

    mixed_precision:            # mixed precision settings for fsdp/fsdp2
      param_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}
      reduce_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}
      buffer_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}

    amp:
      enabled: False                 # if True, automatic mixed precision (AMP) will be used in FSDP/FSDP2 training.
      precision: "bf16"              # precision for AMP, options are ["fp16" , "bf16"]
      use_grad_scaler: False         # if True, GradScaler will be used for AMP training to prevent underflow.

reward:
  use_reward_model: False

critic:

items.title: [Troubleshoot]: GPU ID mismatch, OOM behavior in 'All' mode, and Optimal Configuration
items.body:
### Problem description

I am conducting experiments on a node with 8x NVIDIA H20 GPUs. I have observed three distinct behaviors regarding placement, memory usage, and performance that I would like to report and discuss.

1. **Logical vs. Physical GPU ID Mismatch** 

There is a discrepancy between the configured GPU IDs, the os.environ output, and the actual physical GPU usage. When actor/rollout occupies 0-5:

Config env: 6-7: Actually runs on physical GPUs 0-1.

Config env: 0-1: Actually runs on physical GPUs 6-7 (Ray seems to auto-schedule to idle cards).

Misleading Log: In both cases, os.environ.get('CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES') prints the configured IDs from the YAML, not the actual physical IDs being used.

2. **OOM in 'All' Mode vs. Partial Overlap**

Global Overlap (all): Setting actor, env, rollout: all causes immediate CUDA OOM. It seems the overhead of placing an Env worker on every GPU alongside the Actor is too high.

Partial Overlap: If I limit env to share only specific GPUs with the Actor (e.g., env: 0-5 or env: 0-1), it runs successfully without OOM.

3. **Optimal Configuration & Performance Inquiry** 

To balance sampling speed and memory stability, I settled on the following configuration (overlapping on 0-5):

``` YAML
component_placement:
  actor,rollout: 0-5
  env: 0-5
```
This setup is stable (no OOM) and provides faster sampling than using only the 2 idle GPUs.

Sampling Speed: ~1 minute 30 seconds per rollout epoch.

Estimated Training Time: ~48 hours for 1000 steps.

Is this performance (1.5 min/epoch) considered reasonable/standard for this hardware setup?

### Configuration YAML file

YAML config file:

You can also paste the full config here.
```
defaults:
  - env/train: libero_10
  - env/eval: libero_10
  - override hydra/job_logging: stdout

hydra:
  run:
    dir: .
  output_subdir: null
  searchpath:
    - file://${oc.env:EMBODIED_PATH}/config/

cluster:
  num_nodes: 1
  component_placement:
    actor,rollout: 0-5
    env: 0-5

runner:
  task_type: embodied
  logger:
    log_path: "../results"
    project_name: rlinf
    experiment_name: "test_openpi"
    logger_backends: ["tensorboard"] # wandb, swanlab

  max_epochs: 1000
  max_steps: -1

  val_check_interval: -1
  save_interval: 40
  seq_length: 4096
  max_prompt_length: 50

algorithm:
  auto_reset: False
  ignore_terminations: False
  use_fixed_reset_state_ids: True
  normalize_advantages: True
  kl_penalty: kl  # how to estimate kl divergence: kl or kl_penalty
  group_size: 1
  max_episode_steps: 480
  use_ordered_reset_state_ids: False
  reward_coef: 1.0
  n_chunk_steps: 48
  n_eval_chunk_steps: 48
  num_group_envs: 48
  rollout_epoch: 1
  reward_type: chunk_level
  logprob_type: chunk_level
  entropy_type: token_level

  update_epoch: 4
  adv_type: gae
  loss_type: actor_critic
  loss_agg_func: "token-mean" 
  kl_beta: 0.0
  entropy_bonus: 0

items.title: RoboTwin GRPO rollout too slow; possible weak GPU parallelization of environments
items.body:
### Problem description

We are reproducing OpenVLA-OFT reinforcement learning (GRPO) on RoboTwin. Only the “total_num_envs: 128 -> 32” and "group_size: 8 -> 4" in the default config. With this change, the rollout phase is very slow（30:15 for 1 training step, 8 rollout_epochs）. We suspect that parallel robotwin environment execution on 8*H200 is not scaling well in my conda environment, so rollout becomes the bottleneck. We are looking for the intended way to speed up so that rollout time stays acceptable.

[config.yaml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25186342/config.yaml)

items.title: feat(musa): add e2e tests, install and docker support
items.body:
### Description

Adds the missing pieces for running RLinf on Moore Threads (MUSA) GPUs: e2e CI tests, an install path, Docker support, docs, and the runtime fixes those runs surfaced. The scheduler already recognised `MUSA_GPU`; nothing else did.

- `tests/e2e_tests/embodied/*_musa.yaml` — minimal LIBERO-10 and ManiSkill PPO OpenPI pi05 configs, run through the shared `run.sh` with `osmesa` as its backend argument.
- One `runs-on: musa` job in `embodied-e2e-tests.yml`, beside the ROCm and Ascend jobs, gated by the same `embodied_filter`, creating its venv with `install.sh --platform musa`.
- `install.sh --platform musa` — reuses the image's interpreter, creates the venv with `--system-site-packages`, pins torch to the image's version, and seeds its torch/flash-attn metadata so uv cannot overwrite the MUSA builds.
- `PLATFORM=musa` Docker builds on the Moore Threads training-suite image; all nine `embodied-maniskill_libero` models install there unchanged.
- Fix: `masked_mean`/`masked_sum` passed `axis=None` to `Tensor.mean`/`sum`, rejected by torch-musa.
- Fix: `prepare_actions_for_maniskill` hard-coded `.cuda()`; the envs now move the batch to their own device.
- Fix (from #1366): MCCL options are applied only when torch-musa exposes them; SAC/SFT workers use the platform abstraction, not `torch.cuda`.
- `gr00t_n1d5/musa_patches.py`, beside `npu_patches.py`: GR00T's vendored RADIO code calls `torch.cuda.get_device_capability()`, which raises `Invalid device id` on MUSA. Only that sentinel is needed -- MUSA's flash-attn works, so Ascend's import stub would disable a usable kernel.
- New guide `guides/moore_threads_musa.rst` (EN + ZH), wired into the hardware index and installation page, plus a README news entry (EN + ZH) for the non-NVIDIA accelerators.


### Motivation and Context

MUSA was only reachable by running a hand-patched fork inside a hand-built image, so nothing kept it working. These two e2e configs are the smallest runs that exercise rollout, env stepping and an actor+critic update on MUSA, and both of the code fixes above were found by running them against `main`.

Overlaps with #1366, which introduced `--platform musa`. That PR predates the move to the `rlinf-openpi` PyPI package, so its OpenPI/LeRobot source-install workarounds are no longer needed; its `musa_gpu.py` and worker device-abstraction fixes are carried over here.

### How has this been tested?

On an 8× MTT S5000 host (driver 3.3.5-server), both configs were run against this branch inside `registry.mthreads.com/lgpublic/rlinf:rlinf0.2-maniskill_libero_openpi-0428-jingdong`, on 2 GPUs each. Both reach a completed PPO step:

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `run.sh libero_10_ppo_openpi_pi05_musa osmesa` | pass — 8 trajectories, `actor/grad_norm=22.486`, `critic/value_loss=0.318` |
| `run.sh maniskill_async_ppo_openpi_pi05_musa osmesa` | pass — 2 trajectories, `actor/grad_norm=67.781`, `critic/value_loss=0.210` |

`bash requirements/install.sh --use-mirror --platform musa embodied --model openpi --env maniskill_libero` was run inside `registry.mthreads.com/mcctest/ai/training-suite:v2.1.5-musa4.3.7`. It builds a venv on the image's Python 3.10.12, installs no torch of its own, and afterwards `torch.__version__` is `2.7.1` from `/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages` with `torch.musa.is_available() == True` and 8 devices; `openpi`, `libero` and `mani_skill` all import.

`DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build --build-arg PLATFORM=musa --build-arg BUILD_TARGET=embodied-musa-maniskill_libero` completes and produces `rlinf:embodied-musa-maniskill_libero`. Running that image with `--runtime=mthreads` gives torch 2.7.1 with `torch.musa.is_available() == True` and 8 devices, `mani_skill`/`libero`/`openpi` all importing, `MUJOCO_GL=osmesa` from the venv, and OSMesa present. Its `/opt/venv/openpi` -- a venv built by `install.sh --platform musa` -- runs `tests/e2e_tests/embodied/run.sh libero_10_ppo_openpi_pi05_musa osmesa` to a completed PPO step (8 trajectories, `actor/grad_norm=53.369`, `critic/value_loss=1.699`).

`masked_mean`/`masked_sum` were checked numerically against the previous implementation over `axis` in `{None, 0, -1}` and empty/full/random masks — identical. `ruff check --preview` and `ruff format --check` are clean on the touched files.

### Additional information (optional, e.g., figures and logs):

Open items and caveats:

- ManiSkill on MUSA needs a vendor-patched SAPIEN **and** a matching patched ManiSkill, neither of which is public. Stock `sapien` raises `Failed to find a supported physical device "cpu"`, and the vendor SAPIEN in turn lacks `sapien.sensor.StereoDepthSensor`, which the public ManiSkill `v3.0.0b22` tag imports (the vendor's checkout is the same commit with that import guarded). So `install.sh --platform musa` yields a working LIBERO environment, while ManiSkill has to run in the vendor RLinf image. Documented in the guide; this is why the CI workflow targets the vendor image.
- The MUSA runner is not registered yet: the job needs a self-hosted runner labelled `musa` whose image carries the MUSA stack, in the same way the `rocm` and `ascend` runners work.
- Unrelated bug worth reporting separately: after HuggingFace returned 429, `libero-download-assets --skip-existing` exited 0 with the assets directory essentially empty, and the image only failed later at `FileNotFoundError: .../desk_caddy.xml`. That silent partial success is in `rlinf-libero` and is platform-agnostic.

### Types of changes

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Documentation update (Document-only update)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)

### Checklist:

- [x] My code follows the code style of this project.
- [x] My change requires a change to the documentation.
- [x] I have updated the documentation accordingly.
- [x] I have added tests to cover my changes.
- [x] All new and existing tests passed.

items.title: [Troubleshoot]: CUDA Out of Memory error during training
items.body:
### Problem description

hi @chenkang455, I noticed that you have answered #537  before, and now I am facing the same problem. I used 8 40G A100 and made the following modifications to the parameters according to your suggestions, but OOM still occurs at random positions during the training process. Can you give me some advice?
```
rollout_epoch: 8->4->2
total_num_envs: 128->64->32
micro_batch_size: 32->8->4
global_batch_size: 1024->256
all enable_offload: True
```
I noticed that OOM occurred during the training process for above all parameter configurations. For example, 20 steps, 24 steps..... I wonder if there are some values that were not released during the training process, leading to accumulation? Thank you!

### Configuration YAML file

YAML config file: `examples/embodiment/config/robotwin_click_bell_grpo_lingbotvla.yaml`

You can also paste the full config here.
```
defaults:
  - env/robotwin_click_bell@env.train
  - env/robotwin_click_bell@env.eval
  - model/lingbotvla@actor.model          
  - training_backend/fsdp@actor.fsdp_config
  - override hydra/job_logging: stdout

hydra:
  run:
    dir: .
  output_subdir: null
  searchpath:
    - file://${oc.env:EMBODIED_PATH}/config/

cluster:
  num_nodes: 1
  component_placement:
    actor, env, rollout: 0-7

runner:
  task_type: embodied
  logger:
    log_path: "../results"
    project_name: rlinf
    experiment_name: "robotwin_grpo_lingbotvla"
    logger_backends: ["tensorboard"] # wandb, swanlab

  max_epochs: 1000
  max_steps: -1

  only_eval: False
  val_check_interval: 20
  save_interval: 100

  resume_dir: null # Optional: path to a saved checkpoint directory, such as 'checkpoints/global_step_10'. If not None, it will be used to resume training.
  ckpt_path: null  # Optional: path to a .pt checkpoint. If not None, it will be loaded after the model is instantiated (for evaluation).

algorithm:
  normalize_advantages: True
  kl_penalty: kl  # how to estimate kl divergence: kl or kl_penalty
  group_size: 8
  update_epoch: 2
  rollout_epoch: 4
  eval_rollout_epoch: 1 # set eval_rollout_epoch > 0 when enable runner.only_eval or runner.val_check_interval > 0

  reward_type: action_level
  logprob_type: token_level
  entropy_type: token_level

  adv_type: grpo
  loss_type: actor
  loss_agg_func: "token-mean"
  kl_beta: 0.05
  entropy_bonus: 0.05
  clip_ratio_high: 0.28
  clip_ratio_low: 0.2
  clip_ratio_c: 3.0
  value_clip: 0.2
  huber_delta: 10.0

  gamma: 1.0
  gae_lambda: 0.95

  reward_coef: 5.0
  filter_rewards: False
  rewards_lower_bound: 0.5
  rewards_upper_bound: 4.5

 # params for rollout

    top_p: 1.0

actor:

  training_backend: "fsdp"
  micro_batch_size: 8
  global_batch_size: 256

    model_type: "lingbotvla"
    lingbotvla:

    value_type: ${algorithm.reward_type}  # 'action' or 'token'

    use_proprio: True

    noise_method: "flow_sde"   
    noise_level: 0.7           
    joint_logprob: False       
    action_env_dim: 14         
    add_value_head: False
    safe_get_logprob: False

  optim:
    lr: 1.0e-5
    value_lr: 1.0e-5
    adam_beta1: 0.9
    adam_beta2: 0.999

reward:

items.title: [Troubleshoot]: RL training with pi0.5 and GRPO in RoboTwin is unstable.
items.body:
### Problem description

Using pi0.5 as the VLA, with absolute joint positions as the action space and the action chunk set to 16, GRPO-based RL training in the place_cans_plastic scenario is unstable.

### Configuration YAML file

YAML config file:

You can also paste the full config here.
```
defaults:
  - env/robotwin_place_cans_plasticbox@env.train
  - env/robotwin_place_cans_plasticbox@env.eval
  - model/pi0_5@actor.model
  - training_backend/fsdp@actor.fsdp_config
  - weight_syncer/patch_syncer@weight_syncer
  - override hydra/job_logging: stdout

hydra:
  run:
    dir: .
  output_subdir: null
  searchpath:
    - file://${oc.env:EMBODIED_PATH}/config/

cluster:
  num_nodes: 1
  component_placement:
    actor, env, rollout: 0,1,3,4,5,6

runner:
  task_type: embodied
  logger:
    log_path: "../results"
    project_name: rlinf
    experiment_name: "robotwin_grpo_openpi_pi05"
    logger_backends: ["tensorboard"] # wandb, swanlab

  max_epochs: 1000
  max_steps: -1

  only_eval: False
  val_check_interval: -1
  save_interval: 10

  resume_dir: null # Optional: path to a saved checkpoint directory, such as 'checkpoints/global_step_10'. If not None, it will be used to resume training.
  ckpt_path: null  # Optional: path to a .pt checkpoint. If not None, it will be loaded after the model is instantiated (for evaluation).

algorithm:
  normalize_advantages: True
  kl_penalty: kl  # how to estimate kl divergence: kl or kl_penalty
  group_size: 8
  reward_coef: 1.0

  rollout_epoch: 4
  eval_rollout_epoch: 1 # set eval_rollout_epoch > 0 when enable runner.only_eval or runner.val_check_interval > 0

  reward_type: chunk_level
  logprob_type: chunk_level
  entropy_type: token_level

  update_epoch: 5
  adv_type: grpo
  loss_type: actor
  loss_agg_func: "token-mean" 
  kl_beta: 0.0
  entropy_bonus: 0
  clip_ratio_high: 0.2
  clip_ratio_low: 0.2
  clip_ratio_c: 3.0
  value_clip: 0.2
  huber_delta: 10.0

  gamma: 0.99
  gae_lambda: 0.95

  filter_rewards: True
  rewards_lower_bound: 0.1
  rewards_upper_bound: 0.9
  # params for generation
  sampling_params:
    do_sample: True
    temperature_train: 1.0
    temperature_eval: 0.6
    top_k: 50
    top_p: 1.0
    repetition_penalty: 1.0
    add_BOS: False

  # length argument for autoregressive sampling
  # max length means max amount of tokens to generate
  length_params:
    max_new_token: null
    max_length: 1024
    min_length: 1

env:
  group_name: "EnvGroup"
  enable_offload: True
  # Override the default values in env/robotwin_place_cans_plasticbox
  train:
    total_num_envs: 240
    reward_coef: ${algorithm.reward_coef}
    max_episode_steps: 320
    max_steps_per_rollout_epoch: 320
    group_size: ${algorithm.group_size}
    assets_path: "/data/zsq/RoboTwin"
    seeds_path: ${oc.env:REPO_PATH}/rlinf/envs/robotwin/seeds/train_seeds.json
    center_crop: False
    task_config:
      embodiment: [aloha-agilex]
      camera:
        collect_wrist_camera: true
      domain_randomization:
        random_background: false
        cluttered_table: false
        clean_background_rate: 1
        random_head_camera_dis: 0
        random_table_height: 0
        random_light: false
        crazy_random_light_rate: 0
  eval:
    total_num_envs: 240
    auto_reset: True
    ignore_terminations: True
    max_episode_steps: 320
    reward_coef: ${algorithm.reward_coef}
    max_steps_per_rollout_epoch: 320
    group_size: 1
    use_fixed_reset_state_ids: True
    is_eval: True
    assets_path: "/data/zsq/RoboTwin"
    seeds_path: ${oc.env:REPO_PATH}/rlinf/envs/robotwin/seeds/eval_seeds.json
    video_cfg:
      save_video: True
      video_base_dir: ${runner.logger.log_path}/video/eval
    center_crop: False
    task_config:
      embodiment: [aloha-agilex]
      camera:
        collect_wrist_camera: true
      domain_randomization:
        random_background: false
        cluttered_table: false
        clean_background_rate: 1
        random_head_camera_dis: 0
        random_table_height: 0
        random_light: false
        crazy_random_light_rate: 0

rollout:
  group_name: "RolloutGroup"
  backend: "huggingface"
  recompute_logprobs: False
  enable_offload: True
  pipeline_stage_num: 1
  model:
    model_path: ${actor.model.model_path}
    precision: ${actor.model.precision}

actor:
  group_name: "ActorGroup"
  training_backend: "fsdp"
  micro_batch_size: 40
  global_batch_size: 960 # 1024
  seed: 42
  enable_offload: False

  # Override the default values in model/openpi_pi05
  model:
    model_path: "/data/zsq/pi05_ckpt/robotwin_place_cans_plastic/20000_torch"
    num_action_chunks: 16 # interface for the env
    action_dim: 14
    # add_value_head: True
    num_steps: 5
    use_proprio: True
    openpi_data:
      adapt_to_pi: False
      extra_delta_transform: False
    openpi:
      config_name: pi05_robotwin
      num_images_in_input: 3
      action_chunk: ${actor.model.num_action_chunks}
      action_env_dim: ${actor.model.action_dim}
      num_steps: ${actor.model.num_steps}
      noise_method: "flow_sde"
      noise_level: 0.3
      # value_after_vlm: True
      # detach_critic_input: True

  optim:
    lr: 5.0e-06
    value_lr: 1.0e-04
    adam_beta1: 0.9
    adam_beta2: 0.95
    adam_eps: 1.0e-08
    weight_decay: 0.01
    clip_grad: 1.0
    critic_warmup_steps: 0

  # Override the default values in training_backend/fsdp
  fsdp_config:
    strategy: "fsdp"
    gradient_checkpointing: False # for openpi, gradient checkpointing is not supported, please do not change this value
    mixed_precision:
      param_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}
      reduce_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}
      buffer_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}

reward:
  use_reward_model: False

critic:
  use_critic_model: False
```

items.title: refactor(workers): split EmbodiedFSDPActor into its own module
items.body: ### Description Split `rlinf/workers/actor/fsdp_actor_worker.py` into two modules. `FSDPActor` (reasoning/LLM RL) stays in `fsdp_actor_worker.py` together with `compute_rollout_train_kl`; `EmbodiedFSDPActor` plus its four nested-dict helpers moves to a new `rlinf/workers/actor/embodied_fsdp_actor_worker.py`. - `fsdp_actor_worker.py` shrinks from 1731 to 976 lines; the new `embodied_fsdp_actor_worker.py` is 792 lines. - The helpers `process_nested_dict_for_adv`, `process_nested_dict_for_train`, `trim_nested_tensor_time_dim`, and `flatten_nested_tensor_time_batch` move with `EmbodiedFSDPActor`; `compute_rollout_train_kl` stays with `FSDPActor`. - The eight downstream modules that imported `EmbodiedFSDPActor` from the old path are re-pointed to the new module. No runtime behavior changes. ### Motivation and Context `fsdp_actor_worker.py` held both the reasoning/LLM actor and the embodied actor in one 1731-line file, forcing two unrelated code paths to share a module. Splitting keeps each actor self-contained and the files manageable. ### How has this been tested? - `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on all changed files. - Import smoke test loads `FSDPActor`, `EmbodiedFSDPActor`, all five helpers, and every subclass module (`fsdp_sac_policy_worker`, `fsdp_dagger_policy_worker`, `fsdp_nft_policy_worker`, `fsdp_iql_policy_worker`, `fsdp_actor_worker_pipeline`, `async_ppo_fsdp_worker`, `fsdp_rlt_ac_policy_worker`, `fsdp_inference_worker`). - End-to-end run with `examples/embodiment/config/libero_goal_ppo_openpi_pi05.yaml` (`loss_type: actor_critic`, which drives `EmbodiedFSDPActor` directly), `runner.max_steps=50`, on 4xA800 with the openpi venv and `/mnt/public/hao/models/RLinf-Pi05-LIBERO-SFT`. Completed all 50 steps with zero errors; `env/success_once` went 0.80 -> 0.875 and `train/actor/grad_norm` 12.1 -> 6.5. ### Additional information (optional, e.g. figures and logs) Run command: `python examples/embodiment/train_embodied_agent.py --config-path examples/embodiment/config --config-name libero_goal_ppo_openpi_pi05 actor.model.model_path= rollout.model.model_path= runner.max_steps=50` ### Types of changes - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] Documentation update (Document-only update) - [x] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) ### Checklist: - [x] My code follows the code style of this project. - [ ] My change requires a change to the documentation. - [ ] I have updated the documentation accordingly. - [ ] I have added tests to cover my changes. - [x] All new and existing tests passed.

items.title: perf: overlap bootstrap with training (cpu rendering)
items.body:
Performance Improvement: Asynchronous Environment Bootstrapping and Training Overlap

### Description
~~This PR introduces a new `warmup` method to the `EnvWorker` class to enable asynchronous environment preparation. The `warmup` function is designed to be called prior to `interact`, allowing environment bootstrapping to occur in parallel with `run_training`.
We also add a new `-1` configuration option for environment settings to explicitly denote CPU-only physics and rendering, and the function `get_group_accelerators` in `embodied_runner.py` to check if there is resource overlap.~~
Updated the PR based on feedback and copied suggested changes. Main difference is that warmup is not a function but an async handle (it is not called warmup anymore) and class member holding the bootstrap data is freed after consumption (e.g. set to `None`). 
There is also a new configuration for `runner`, `overlap_env_bootstrap`. This parameter needs to be set to True in the yaml file:
```
runner:
     overlap_env_bootstrap: True
``` 

### Motivation and Context
Currently, environment bootstrap time accounts for a significant portion (5%–20%) of each global step. In hardware configurations where `EnvWorker` processes do not compete for resources with the training actor (e.g., CPU-based rendering vs. NPU/GPU-based training), this bootstrap latency can be masked by overlapping it with the training phase.

While the initial global step time remains unchanged, subsequent steps see significant improvement in throughput.
*Preliminary Results:*
In a CPU + NPU environment (benchmarked on `libero_10` with Pi0.5 and PPO, with changes for minimal configuration), we observed a reduction in per-global-step time from 720s to approximately 620–640s.

### How has this been tested?
Validation is ongoing on our internal clusters using standard RLinf examples. Specifically:
Execution Script: `run_embodiment.sh`
Configuration: `libero_10_ppo_openpi_pi05.yaml` (with some selected minor adjustments from [Section 2.4 Minimum Test Case](https://rlinf.readthedocs.io/en/latest/rst_source/examples/embodied/pi0.html)).

### Additional information (optional, e.g., figures and logs):
Initial performance figures are posted in [comment](https://github.com/RLinf/RLinf/pull/942#issuecomment-4145842761).
_Further logs and performance figures will be attached upon completion of the test run._

items.title: [Troubleshoot]: IsaacLab + PP0 + GR00T reward and success rate always 0.0
items.body:
### Problem description

Hi, I am attempting to train GR00T in the IsaacLab simulator using the provided RLinf tutorial (https://rlinf.readthedocs.io/en/latest/rst_source/examples/embodied/isaaclab.html), the reward and success rate remain at 0.0 throughout training.

**System Environment**
- docker: rlinf/rlinf:agentic-rlinf0.1-isaaclab
- venv: gr00t
- pre-trained model: https://huggingface.co/RLinf/RLinf-Gr00t-SFT-Spatial
- yaml file: RLinf/examples/embodiment/config/isaaclab_franka_stack_cube_ppo_gr00t_demo.yaml
- command: bash examples/embodiment/run_embodiment.sh isaaclab_franka_stack_cube_ppo_gr00t_demo

I tried two things to fix this training problem:
1. Modify RLinf/examples/embodiment/config/isaaclab_franka_stack_cube_ppo_gr00t_demo.yaml
1.1 Add
      ```yaml
      actor:
        model:
          rl_head_config:
            safe_get_logprob: True
      ```
      to enable PyTorch's numerically stable Normal.log_prob()

   1.2 The config had `use_fixed_reset_state_ids: True`, but `IsaaclabBaseEnv.update_reset_state_ids()` (`isaaclab_env.py:250`) is a stub that does nothing. No demonstration data exists for the IsaacLab stack-cube task, so environments reset to undefined states and objects may spawn in unreachable positions. So I changed the yaml config:
    ```yaml
    env:
      train:
        use_fixed_reset_state_ids: False   # was True; uses IsaacLab's built-in randomized resets
      eval:
        use_fixed_reset_state_ids: False   # was True
    ```
2. `convert_to_isaaclab_stack_cube_action()` in `rlinf/models/embodiment/gr00t/simulation_io.py` applied `np.sign()` directly to the unnormalized gripper value:
      ```
      model output
          → unapply_transforms()          # maps to metadata range: gripper ∈ [0.0, 1.0]
          → np.sign(x ∈ (0, 1])          # always +1
          → IsaacLab receives +1          # always OPEN
      ```
      Because `unapply_transforms()` maps the gripper back to the metadata statistics range (`min=0.0, max=1.0`), the result is always non-negative, so `np.sign()` returns `+1` (open) unconditionally. The robot could never close its gripper.
      The docstring even acknowledged the difference ("gripper in Libero is 0 and 1, but in IsaacLab Stack Cube is −1 and +1") but the implementation skipped the remapping step.
      **Fix** (`rlinf/models/embodiment/gr00t/simulation_io.py`):
      ```python
      # Before:
      action_array[..., -1] = np.sign(action_array[..., -1])
      # After (same as Libero):
      action_array = normalize_gripper_action(action_array, binarize=True)
      ```

While the implemented modifications successfully mitigated numerical instabilities—specifically the inf values in actor/grad_norm and anomalies in actor/ratio and actor/approx_kl—the model has yet to show improvement in performance. Both the reward and success rate remain stagnant at 0.0. I would appreciate your insights into what might be preventing the agent from initiating the learning process.

### Configuration YAML file

YAML config file: RLinf/examples/embodiment/config/isaaclab_franka_stack_cube_ppo_gr00t_demo.yaml

You can also paste the full config here.
```
defaults:
  - env/isaaclab_stack_cube@env.train
  - env/isaaclab_stack_cube@env.eval
  - model/gr00t@actor.model
  - training_backend/fsdp@actor.fsdp_config
  - override hydra/job_logging: stdout

hydra:
  run:
    dir: .
  output_subdir: null
  searchpath:
    - file://${oc.env:EMBODIED_PATH}/config/

cluster:
  num_nodes: 1
  component_placement:
      env: 2
      rollout:
        node_group: "rollout"
        placement: 3
      actor: 2-3

  node_groups:
    - label: "rollout"
      node_ranks: all
      env_configs:
        - node_ranks: all
          env_vars:
            # The gr00t model contains numerous numpy operations, whose performance is sensitive to the OMP_NUM_THREADS environment variable.
            # By default, this is set to 1 by Ray. Consider increasing it to improve performance.
            # Recommended to increase to number of CPU cores (use lscpu to check) divided by rollout world size.
            # Do not set this globally in the shell script which will increase the number of threads for all processes,
            # because PyTorch performance will be degraded, contrary to numpy.
            - OMP_NUM_THREADS: 1

runner:
  task_type: embodied
  logger:
    log_path: "../results"
    project_name: rlinf
    experiment_name: "isaaclab_ppo_gr00t_demo"
    logger_backends: ["tensorboard"] # wandb, swanlab

  max_epochs: 200

  only_eval: False

  entropy_type: chunk_level

    use_fixed_reset_state_ids: False
    video_cfg:
      save_video: True
      info_on_video: True
      video_base_dir: ${runner.logger.log_path}/video/eval

rollout:
  group_name: "RolloutGroup"
  backend: "huggingface"
  enable_offload: True
  pipeline_stage_num: 2

  model:
    model_path: "/root/RLinf/model/RLinf-Gr00t-SFT-Spatial/"
    precision: ${actor.model.precision}

actor:
  group_name: "ActorGroup"
  training_backend: "fsdp"
  micro_batch_size: 8
  global_batch_size: 16
  seed: 1234
  enable_offload: False

  # Override the default values in model/gr00t
  model:
    model_path: "/root/RLinf/model/RLinf-Gr00t-SFT-Spatial/"
    add_value_head: True
    embodiment_tag: "isaaclab_franka"
    obs_converter_type: "isaaclab_stack_cube"
    num_action_chunks: 16
    rl_head_config:
      safe_get_logprob: True

  optim:
    lr: 2.0e-5
    value_lr: 2.0e-5
    adam_beta1: 0.9
    adam_beta2: 0.95
    adam_eps: 1.0e-08
    clip_grad: 1.0
    weight_decay: 0.01
    critic_warmup_steps: 0
  
  # Override the default values in training_backend/fsdp
  fsdp_config:
    strategy: "fsdp"
    gradient_checkpointing: True
    mixed_precision:
      param_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}
      reduce_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}
      buffer_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}

reward:
  use_reward_model: False

critic:
  use_critic_model: False

```

You can find the log file in `logs/` folder or the $output_dir/$experiment_name folder (defined in the yaml config) if you are using our example scripts.

items.body:
### Description

- Train the single-token SFP trajectory-velocity objective using real episode-level `action_states`, scale-only normalization, and reproducible optimizer-step time/noise slicing across micro-batches.
- Add LIBERO conversion and normalization-statistics tools, SFP model/data configurations, and English/Chinese training documentation. `action_states` uses a copy of the actions statistics.
- Add a chunk-synchronous SFP evaluation sampler that carries action state across chunks and resets it on explicit episode starts. SFP requires Pi0.5; RL, DAgger, DSRL, and RTC are rejected.

The branch includes upstream main through `30e02369`, including unified OpenPI, the cross-shard gradient-norm fix, and OpenPI sharding/mixed-precision updates. The conflict resolution preserves activation checkpointing, retains SFP random-input slicing, and skips unused final prefix outputs in the SFP loss. Common FSDP/optimizer implementations and non-SFP Gemma/SigLIP/checkpoint code have no additional changes relative to that main.

### Motivation and Context

StreamingVLA trains on cumulative action trajectories, which require action states and scale-only normalization. An opt-in objective on the shared OpenPI implementation adds these semantics while retaining the existing model factory and worker interfaces.

### How has this been tested?

Validation of this merge on CPU:

- Run each file in a separate pytest process with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""`, `OMP_NUM_THREADS=2`, and `PYTHONPATH=$PWD`: `test_models.py` (77 passed, 1 skipped), `test_data.py -k 'not test_vlm_trend_batch_video_metadata_stays_nested_per_sample'` (130 passed, 7 skipped, 1 deselected), and `test_fsdp.py` (89 passed, 1 skipped). The FSDP suite includes real CPU wrapper forward/backward, gradient-reduction group selection, and SFP activation-checkpointing coverage.
- The deselected VideoMetadata test fails identically on clean main with this server's Transformers version (`frames_indices` constructor incompatibility). A first combined-file run also encountered mock module pollution; the file-isolated CI execution passes the affected collector cases.
- Fixed-input small-model comparison against the pre-merge PR source: fp32 and bf16 SFP loss, all 98 parameter gradients, and `action_out_proj` AdamW updates are identical, with and without non-reentrant activation checkpointing. This uses reduced Gemma/SigLIP models, not the production checkpoint.
- The official `train_vla_sft.py --config-name libero_sft_pi05_sfp --cfg job --resolve` entrypoint resolves successfully with SFP, 100,000 steps, 5,000-step saving, and activation checkpointing enabled.
- `pre-commit run --all-files`, Ruff, format, and `git diff --check` pass. The docs-check harness builds both languages with zero reported warnings; the RST markup checker reports no issues.

All eight GPUs were occupied, so the merged tree has not received a new production-checkpoint GPU smoke or 100-step run.

Those results describe the earlier validation run; the current merge validation is listed above.

items.title: fix(fsdp): reduce the gradient norm over every shard
items.body:
### Description

`create_device_mesh` builds a 1-D mesh whose only dimension is named `fsdp`, so the `"ddp" in mesh_dim_names` guard on `_dp_group` never matched and the group stayed `None` for every FSDP and FSDP2 run. `get_grad_norm` skipped its `all_reduce` as a result and returned the norm of whichever shard the local rank held, which `clip_grad_norm_` then clipped against.

The selection now lives in a named `gradient_reduction_group(device_mesh)` rather than inline in the manager, because it carries a constraint that is easy to get wrong: the group has to span the sharding dimension and nothing else. Hybrid sharding replicates across `ddp`, so reducing over that dimension would count each shard once per replica.

### Motivation and Context

The reported norm was roughly `1/sqrt(world_size)` of the real one and shrank as the job grew, so gradient clipping silently loosened with scale. A two-GPU measurement from #1498 puts numbers on it: without the reduction `grad_norm` came out 50.6862 against a reference DDP value of 71.9728 (≈ 1/√2); with it, 72.0690.

**This changes training behaviour for every existing FSDP config.** Clipping now bites at the configured threshold, so runs that were effectively unclipped will now be clipped even though nothing in their YAML moved. That is the intended correction, but it is worth knowing before rerunning a baseline.

Overlaps with #1522, which reaches the same `_dp_group = mesh["fsdp"].get_group()` while adding the 2-D hybrid mesh. The two agree on the value; whichever lands second should take the other's version of the line.

### How has this been tested?

- `tests/unit_tests/test_fsdp_device_mesh_timeout.py` gains a case pinning which mesh dimension the group comes from, including the loud failure when no sharding dimension exists — silently reducing over the wrong one is how this went unnoticed.
- Full file: 10 passed. Note this file is order-sensitive on a busy machine; its real `init_process_group` tests race for ephemeral ports and fail intermittently on `main` as well.
- The cross-rank reduction itself needs more than one rank and is **not** covered by a unit test. A 2-rank gloo spawn test does cover it but costs ~60s and polluted the other tests in the file, so it was dropped in favour of the two-GPU measurement above.

items.title: fix(embodiment): sum joint log-probs over denoising chain instead of averaging in pi0RL
items.body:
### Description

With `joint_logprob=True`, pi0RL aggregated the K+1 log-probability terms (initial Gaussian + K conditional denoising steps) with `mean(dim=1)` on both the rollout collection side (`rlinf/models/embodiment/openpi/tasks/rl.py:286`) and the actor recompute side (`rlinf/models/embodiment/openpi/tasks/rl.py:497-498`). This commit changes both `mean(dim=1)` aggregations to `sum(dim=1)`. The NFT/non-joint paths and the value-head aggregation (`rl.py:507`) are unchanged.

### Motivation and Context

Fixes #1804. For a Markovian chain the joint log-probability is the sum of the conditional terms. Averaging instead of summing makes the PPO importance ratio become `r^(1/(K+1))`, which effectively relaxes clipping and distorts gradient magnitude. Claim comment: https://github.com/RLinf/RLinf/issues/1804#issuecomment-6595264175 (includes AI-assistance disclosure). At claim time the timeline check confirmed no in-flight PR for this issue from this account.

### How has this been tested?

Code-level + math-level verification only; full GPU training is not runnable on this machine and was not run.

1. `timeout 120 python -c` torch numeric check: `sum == mean*(K+1)` → `True`; `r_avg == r_joint**(1/(K+1))` → `True` (K=4).
2. `timeout 300 python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/test_models.py -k 'pi0 or rl'` → `1 passed, 79 deselected`.
3. `timeout 300 python -m pytest tests/unit_tests -k 'pi0 or rl' --ignore=tests/unit_tests/test_placement --ignore=tests/unit_tests/test_real_env --continue-on-collection-errors` (the `--ignore` flags are needed because those dirs fail collection with missing dependencies) → `7 failed, 14 passed, 4 skipped`. All 7 failures are in `test_channel.py` (6) and `test_robotics.py` (1) — modules untouched by this diff — and the same FAILURES appear on a clean tree (stash), so they are environment/slow-test issues, not introduced by this fix.

items.title: [Bug]: pi0RL implementation averages log-probabilities over denoising steps instead of summing
items.body:
### Affected component

rlinf/models/embodiment/openpi/tasks/rl.py

Specifically, the Flow-Noise implementation with joint_logprob=True in _predict_train() and default_forward().

### Bug description

I noticed that when joint_logprob=True, the implementation averages log-probabilities across denoising steps rather than summing them, in order to compute a log-probability of the denoising chain to run PPO:

```
if rl_cfg.joint_logprob:
    log_probs_picked = log_probs_stacked.mean(dim=1)
```

My understanding is that, for a Markovian denoising chain, the joint log-probability should be the sum of the conditional log-probabilities across denoising steps:

[
\log p_\theta(x_{0}\mid s)
= \log p(x_0) + \sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\log p_\theta(x_{k+1}\mid x_k,s).
]

Averaging instead of summing changes the PPO importance ratio. Since the implementation also includes the initial Gaussian sample, for (K) denoising steps this effectively gives

[
r_{\mathrm{avg}} = r_{\mathrm{joint}}^{1/(K+1)}
]

assuming the initial-noise distribution is policy-independent.

This is no longer the true joint-chain importance ratio, and it effectively relaxes PPO's clipping while changing the gradient magnitude.

I am wondering if this was intentional or whether this was ablated?

Thanks for the clarification!

### Configuration YAML file

YAML config file:

```
algorithm:
  reward_type: chunk_level
  logprob_type: chunk_level
  entropy_type: chunk_level
  clip_ratio_high: 0.2
  clip_ratio_low: 0.2

actor:
  model:
    num_action_chunks: 5
    num_steps: 4
    openpi:
      task: rl
      config_name: "pi05_maniskill"
      noise_method: "flow_noise"
      action_horizon: 8
      noise_params: [0.16, 0.12, 200]
      joint_logprob: True
```


### Log file

N/A

N/A

items.title: fix(fsdp): reject incompatible master optimizer state
items.body:
### Description

Reject populated low-precision AdamW checkpoints that lack FP32 master weights when restoring FP32MasterAdamW. Previously, these states loaded successfully but subsequent updates fell back to the low-precision model parameters. The check runs before changing optimizer state and tells users how to resume with the original optimizer or start a new optimizer from model weights.

- Preserve valid master checkpoint restore and subsequent updates.
- Extend the existing FSDP component tests with FP32 reference comparisons, accumulation, clipping, and checkpoint round trips.
- Document the optional optimizer, memory cost, and checkpoint requirements in the English and Chinese Pi0 guides. Native AdamW and shipped defaults remain unchanged.

### Motivation and Context

Related to #1649 and the optimizer introduced in #1493. Non-LoRA FP32 master support is now available on main through #1667. This PR preserves that implementation and its per-wrapper mixed precision policies; the remaining change covers checkpoint validation, regression tests, and Pi0 usage documentation.

Restoring native BF16 optimizer state into FP32MasterAdamW does not reconstruct missing master weights. Valid master checkpoints remain supported; switching from native BF16 requires loading model weights and starting a new optimizer, not an exact optimizer resume.

### How has this been tested?

- After merging main `d80cf00` on 2026-10-31, `pytest tests/unit_tests/test_fsdp.py -q`: 106 passed, 1 skipped on CPU, Python 3.12.3 / PyTorch 2.11.0. The skipped upstream test requires two CUDA GPUs. Tests cover small updates against an independent PyTorch FP32 AdamW reference, gradient accumulation and clipping, BF16/FP16/FP32 parameters, and checkpoint restore followed by another update.
- Before this main integration (2026-10-10), two-rank CUDA FSDP1 `no_shard`: `use_orig_params=False/True` crossed with `local_shard/dcp`, all four combinations passed on two RTX 5090 GPUs with PyTorch 2.11.0+cu129. These use a small constructed model; FP32 reference agreement and restored optimizer/scheduler state are checked separately from Pi0 training.
- Before this main integration (2026-10-10), real Pi0/LIBERO training on two RTX 5090 GPUs: native AdamW and FP32 master each completed six iterations / 120 optimizer updates. The master run resumed from iteration 6 and completed iteration 8 / optimizer update 160. Master checkpoints contain all 108 FP32 master tensors (311,427,072 elements), including after resume. All recorded scalar metrics were finite.

- English and Chinese Sphinx builds with `-W --keep-going`: passed. `pre-commit run --all-files`: passed.

The integrated revision passed the CPU suite and both strict documentation builds. GPU and Pi0 results below are from the pre-integration revision; those runs were not repeated for this merge. GitHub Actions checks require maintainer approval; that status is not a test failure.

| Measurement | Native, lr=5e-6 | Master, lr=5e-6 | Master, lr=5e-7 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| BF16 trainable weights changed between updates 60 and 120 | 0.9504% | 15.6478% | 1.6325% |
| Largest sampled device-memory peak across two GPUs (MiB) | 21,990 | 24,553 | 24,557 |
| Median actor training time, iterations 2–6 (seconds) | 20.51 | 22.29 | 21.72 |
| Reported approximate KL range over six iterations | 0.0422–0.0662 | 0.2946–1.2928 | -0.0090–0.0578 |

The additional master run changes only actor learning rate to 5e-7 and also completes six iterations / 120 optimizer updates. Device memory was sampled once per second with `nvidia-smi`; it is not a PyTorch allocator peak. These timings describe these runs, not a general throughput benchmark.

Retaining small updates changes the effective optimization: the original learning rate produces larger approximate KL with master weights; the smaller-rate run supports checking learning rate when opting in. This does not select a generally optimal learning rate. The 50-step short episodes record `env/success_once=0` in every configuration, so these runs validate updates and checkpoint use rather than task convergence.

![Pi0 short training traces](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cyanseek/RLinf/86509c45729884aad626afb88c71b59ad2498fda/pi0-training.png)


### Additional information (optional, e.g., figures and logs):

In the controlled small-update test, 1,000 updates at learning rate 5e-6 leave native BF16 weights at 1.0. The FP32 master equals the independent FP32 AdamW reference at 0.9949336051940918; its BF16 model weight is 0.99609375.

<details>
<summary>Pi0 validation configuration</summary>

The configuration starts from `tests/e2e_tests/embodied/libero_spatial_ppo_openpi.yaml` at main `0067f7d`. Both runs use `RLinf/RLinf-Pi0-LIBERO-Spatial-Object-Goal-SFT` revision `4ec11623fba96e1432e535e2c76a634a5e0bdb96`, actor seed 42, environment seed 0, native parameter dtypes, no LoRA, and the existing `train_expert_only=True` setting. The VLM stays frozen. Default learning rates, noise level 0.5, four denoising steps, and five action chunks are retained.

Overrides: six runner iterations; four training environments; 50 steps per rollout epoch and per episode; two rollout epochs; actor microbatch 1 / global batch 4; critic warmup 0; actor and rollout offload enabled; tracer and video disabled; checkpoint every three iterations; `save_full_model_weights=False`. Native and master differ only in `actor.optim.use_fp32_master_params`. The master checkpoint at iteration 6 is resumed with `runner.max_epochs=8`.

The environment uses Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu129, Ray 2.59.0, rlinf-openpi 0.1.1, rlinf-libero 0.1.3, NumPy 1.26.4, and PyArrow 23.0.0, built through `requirements/install.sh embodied --model openpi --env libero --torch 2.11.0 --no-root --no-flash-attn`. Each driver starts an isolated local Ray cluster; model, rollout, training, and checkpoint code use the normal embodied entry point.

</details>

items.title: feat(algorithms): add GSPO for reasoning
items.body:
### Description

Add the original GSPO sequence objective to the reasoning policy-loss registry. Each response uses the exponential of its mean valid-token log-probability difference, sequence-level clipping, and an equal share of the batch loss. The existing GRPO estimator supplies group-relative advantages. Existing PPO/GRPO defaults remain unchanged.

Include an FSDP example, English and Chinese algorithm documentation, component tests, and a GSPO configuration in the existing FSDP/SGLang reasoning e2e workflow. Validate incompatible objective settings and invalid clipping widths before cluster startup. The example links rollout/tokenizer paths to the actor path, uses fp32 actor parameters with bf16 forward computation, and links the old-probability recomputation microbatch to the training microbatch. Document the actual microbatch setting and separate checkpoint evaluation.

### Motivation and Context

Related to #1221 and the contribution roadmap #1322. This implements GSPO only; DRPO remains separate, so this PR does not close the combined request. The objective follows equations 5–7 of [Group Sequence Policy Optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.18071), rather than its GSPO-token variant.

### How has this been tested?

Update (2026-10-31): merged main `d80cf00` and resolved the test-file conflict while retaining both GSPO and the upstream LingBot-VLA v2 cases. `pytest -q tests/unit_tests/test_models.py tests/unit_tests/test_utils.py` passed on CPU (148 passed, 1 optional-dependency skip). Ruff lint/format checks passed. The GSPO objective, example configurations and bilingual algorithm pages are unchanged.


- CPU: `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/test_models.py tests/unit_tests/test_utils.py -q --timeout=90` — **128 passed, 1 skipped** with Python 3.12.3 and PyTorch 2.11.0+cpu. The skip is an existing optional Gemma3 import test. The original missing-loss cases and five newly rejected clipping settings were reproduced as failures before implementation.
- Tests cover independent float64 loss/gradient references, both clipping signs, padding with nonfinite values, empty responses, equal rewards, variable lengths, fixed microbatch accumulation, and sequence versus token clipping. Both Hydra configurations are composed with group sizes 2/4/8, clipping fallbacks, different microbatches/precisions, rollout log probabilities, and optional KL/entropy. Focused command: `python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/test_models.py tests/unit_tests/test_utils.py -k gspo -q`.
- GPU numerical checks on an RTX 5090, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu128: shapes `(8,17)`, `(8,1024)`, `(4,8192)` matched an independent float64 reference, with maximum absolute loss error `4.90e-8` and gradient error `4.95e-10`. Twenty-seven additional common-domain cases matched the extracted verl GSPO/aggregation functions and the sequence-ratio/GRPO-reduction objective transcribed from TRL source: maximum loss difference `7.45e-8`, gradient difference `7.45e-9`. Sources: [verl](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/396e29856c899acf1a490a8927a6604205bd2d7c/verl/trainer/ppo/core_algos.py) and [TRL](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/0e7bb367e4fc597004b4445df24d88b8caa9eaf5/trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py). Nine additional advantage-estimation cases (group sizes 2/4/8; equal, binary and continuous rewards) matched the extracted verl function exactly. This checks first-order objectives and the shared advantage convention, not complete trainers; TRL uses a different normalization epsilon, and different empty-response handling, extra corrections, and numerical clamps are outside the comparison.
- **Actual Ray/SGLang/FSDP pipeline:** two RTX 4090 GPUs, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu129, Ray 2.58.0, SGLang 0.5.12.post1 and Transformers 5.6.1. An adapted configuration with Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, public GSM8K, seed 1234, 512 response tokens, fp32 actor parameters and bf16 forward/rollout completed: two normal rollout iterations with checkpoint save; resume from iteration 2 through 4; group size 4 with rollout-provided old probabilities and clipping 0.01/0.02; and nonzero KL/entropy coefficients. Each case had finite, nonzero optimizer gradients. A strict checkpoint reload confirmed 290 independent parameter tensors changed from initialization.
- The pipeline uses the unchanged reasoning training entry point and public algorithm registry. Local launch instrumentation isolates the Ray cluster and pins SGLang's otherwise-unforwarded sampling seed. A separate evaluation harness uses actual RLinf Ray rollout/reward workers because the reasoning training loop does not currently execute held-out evaluation from `val_check_interval`.
- **Matched 200-iteration training comparison completed:** each method generated 12,800 responses and performed 400 optimizer updates, with 16 prompts × group size 4, two minibatches, training/recomputation microbatch 2, learning rate `1e-6`, and the same seed/model/data/precision. GSPO uses clipping `0.0003/0.0004`; the sequence-mean GRPO control uses `0.2/0.2`. Fixed 256-question greedy evaluation scored initial **121/256 (47.27%)**, GSPO at iteration 200 **130/256 (50.78%)**, and GRPO at iteration 200 **129/256 (50.39%)**. All nine baseline/checkpoint evaluations contain the same 256 unique questions. The one-question final difference does not support GSPO superiority (paired exact McNemar p=1); neither curve improves monotonically. The separately reported 1,000-iteration continuation and full test evaluation also completed; the continuation started from 200, not the best subset checkpoint.
- The full pipeline exposed an important numerical configuration issue: using training/recomputation microbatches 2/1 produced a first-minibatch clipping fraction of 0.28125 before any parameter update. Matching both to 2 gave ratio 1, approximate KL 0 and clipping fraction 0 in the first minibatch of all 998 logged GSPO rollouts across the initial and resumed runs. Both public configurations now link these settings, with regression assertions and bilingual guidance.
- **Resumed stability validation:** GSPO completed 1,000 rollout iterations / 2,000 optimizer updates / 64,000 generated responses, including resume at 200 and two training-epoch boundaries. All recorded scalars across 1,996 logged updates were finite (the upstream runner does not emit the last rollout of either invocation). Checkpoints 400/600/800/1000 passed strict reload and retained changed tensors after bf16 export; saved dataloader positions matched the 467-batch epochs. Fixed 256-question scores at 400/600/800/1000 were 134/136/138/138. This validates sustained execution and the measured learning trajectory, not universal convergence.
- **Full GSM8K test:** the same 1,319 unique questions, greedy decoding and 512-token limit scored initial **644/1319 (48.82%)**, GSPO 200 **694/1319 (52.62%)**, GRPO 200 **652/1319 (49.43%)**, and GSPO 1000 **743/1319 (56.33%)**. Twenty-five appended padding examples were excluded by retaining the first result per unique prompt. These are one-seed integration measurements, not a reproduction of the paper's large MoE benchmark or evidence of general superiority. GSPO 1000 has a larger training budget than the GRPO control.
- **Repeatability limitation:** the 256 shared questions had 19/18/15/6 reward disagreements between the subset and full-test runs for initial/GSPO200/GRPO200/GSPO1000, respectively. Model paths and sampling settings match, and `do_sample=False` maps to temperature zero. Greedy engine execution is therefore not bitwise reproducible in this setup; the cause is not isolated. Reported scores describe these actual runs, and question-paired statistics do not quantify engine or training-run variability.
- English and Chinese Sphinx builds: zero warnings. Changed documentation pages pass inline-markup and code-symbol checks. `pre-commit run --all-files`, commit-message/signoff checks and `git diff --check` pass.

The repository's exact 1.5B e2e preset remains for maintainer-enabled CI; the executed full-pipeline configuration uses the smaller model and public dataset described above. Multi-node, Megatron, MoE, multi-seed robustness and convergence beyond the measured 1,000-iteration trajectory are not established. No end-to-end speedup or general algorithm-quality improvement is claimed.

### Additional information

The supported input is a complete reasoning response with fixed-size microbatches. Empty responses contribute zero policy loss and gradient while retaining their batch denominator slot. Optional entropy/reference-KL terms retain the existing actor reductions and require nonempty response masks; both coefficients are zero in the example. The clipping values `0.0003/0.0004` follow the paper's experiment and are not claimed to be optimal for every model or dataset.

(2) Support gradient norm clipping with mixed-precision gradients. Mainly follows the official PyTorch FSDP implementation ([FullyShardedDataParallel source](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/torch/distributed/fsdp/fully_sharded_data_parallel.py#L1070-L1218)). Experimental evaluation on LIBERO-Goal using π₀ shows that both the training curves and training metrics are consistent with the original results. The original `no_shard` mode also runs correctly. Full-parameter fine-tuning can improve the success rate. ### Additional information (optional, e.g., figures and logs): ### Types of changes - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] Documentation update (Document-only update) - [x] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) ### Checklist: - [ ] My code follows the code style of this project. - [ ] My change requires a change to the documentation. - [ ] I have updated the documentation accordingly. - [ ] I have added tests to cover my changes. - [ ] All new and existing tests passed.
